screening_decisions.reason: RCT with 42 adults with frozen shoulder. Compares intra-articular steroids, mobilisations (manual therapy), ice therapy, and no treatment. All patients taught pendular exercises. Meets criteria: RCT, adults with adhesive capsulitis, compares manual therapy (mobilisations) plus exercise (pendular) with other interventions. Outcomes include pain and range of movement.
Observational study on incidence and management of shoulder disorders in general practice. Not an RCT or quasi-randomised trial.
Educational article describing principles of joint mobilization, not a clinical trial. Not an RCT or quasi-RCT.

Open RCT comparing physical therapies (therapeutic exercises, TENS, IRR) alone vs physical therapies plus arthrography with intra-articular steroid in patients with frozen shoulder. Includes exercise as part of the intervention. Meets criteria for RCT, population, and exercise component.
Systematic review of cohorts of RCTs examining selective reporting. Not a primary study on adhesive capsulitis treatment.

RCT investigating deep transverse friction massage (manual therapy) and capsular stretching (exercise) in idiopathic adhesive capsulitis. Meets criteria for study design, population (adhesive capsulitis), and interventions.

RCT with 29 adults with frozen shoulder. Compares two different exercise programs (glenohumeral ROM exercises vs glenohumeral plus scapulothoracic exercises). Both groups received standard care. Meets criteria: RCT, population, and comparison of different exercise interventions; outcomes include pain, function, ROM.

RCT with 28 subjects with frozen shoulder syndrome. Compares three mobilization techniques (end-range, mid-range, mobilization with movement). Meets criteria: RCT, relevant population, compares different types of manual therapy; outcomes include function and kinematics.

Study comparing PNF movement patterns (a form of exercise) with conventional exercises for chronic peri-arthritis (frozen shoulder). The abstract does not explicitly state randomization, but the study is likely a comparative clinical trial. Conservative approach: include. Exercise interventions in relevant population; outcomes include ROM.

RCT (block randomization) with 15 participants with primary adhesive capsulitis. Compares antero-posterior vs postero-anterior glide mobilizations (manual therapy). Meets criteria: RCT, population (adhesive capsulitis), compares different mobilization techniques; outcomes include ROM and pain.
Cross-sectional prevalence study in the general population. Not an RCT or quasi-RCT on adhesive capsulitis treatment.
This is a case report (7 patients) describing end-range mobilization techniques. No control group. Not an RCT or quasi-RCT.

RCT with 93 subjects with adhesive capsulitis. Compares corticosteroid injection, supervised physiotherapy (includes manual therapy/exercise), combination, and placebo. All taught home exercise. Meets criteria: RCT, relevant population, compares manual therapy/exercise intervention; outcomes include pain, disability, ROM.

RCT with 156 participants with adhesive capsulitis. Compares manual therapy and directed exercise versus placebo (sham ultrasound) following joint distension. Meets criteria: RCT, population, manual therapy and exercise intervention; outcomes include pain, function, movement, quality of life.
Observational study evaluating a questionnaire's responsiveness. Not an RCT on treatment of adhesive capsulitis.
Study of 75 frozen shoulder patients assigned to physical therapy, acupuncture, or both. No mention of randomisation or quasi-randomisation. Doesn't meet design criteria.
Systematic review and cost-effectiveness analysis, not a primary RCT.

Study comparing anterior vs posterior glides (mobilization techniques) for adhesive capsulitis. The abstract suggests comparative design, but full details limited. Included as likely comparative trial of manual therapy. Meets criteria for population and intervention; study design uncertain but conservative inclusion.
Meta-epidemiological study on outcome reporting bias. Not a primary RCT on adhesive capsulitis treatment.
Title suggests relevance but abstract describes a study on multiple sclerosis. Mismatch; does not address adhesive capsulitis treatment.

RCT with 87 patients with frozen shoulder. Compares corticosteroid injection, physiotherapy (includes manual therapy/exercise), and combination. Meets criteria: RCT, relevant population, manual therapy/exercise arm; outcomes include SPADI, ROM.

RCT with 40 patients with adhesive capsulitis. Compares Cyriax approach (deep friction massage and mobilisation exercises) versus conventional physical therapy (hot pack, diathermy, stretching). Both include manual therapy/exercise. Meets criteria.
Prospective observational study of natural history without intervention comparison. Not an RCT.
Methodological paper on heterogeneity measures in meta-analysis. Not a primary study on adhesive capsulitis.
Book chapter from the Cochrane Handbook. Not a primary study.
Prospective cohort study following natural history of frozen shoulder. Not an RCT of intervention.

RCT with 20 patients with painfully restricted shoulders (adhesive capsulitis). Compares passive mobilization plus active exercises vs active exercises alone. Meets criteria: RCT, relevant population, compares manual therapy + exercise; outcomes include pain and mobility.

RCT with 95 shoulders with adhesive capsulitis. Randomised to SH injection, steroid injection, physical therapy modalities, or control. Physical therapy likely includes exercise. Meets criteria: RCT, population, includes exercise; outcomes include pain, ROM, function.
Observational EMG study during exercises in subjects with and without shoulder pathology. Not an RCT comparing treatment interventions.

Compares suprascapular nerve block, corticosteroid injection, and physiotherapy for chronic shoulder pain, not specifically adhesive capsulitis. Condition not clearly defined and may include diverse causes.

RCT with 20 patients with adhesive capsulitis. Compares local steroid injection vs physical therapy (includes exercise). Meets criteria: RCT, population, exercise intervention; outcomes include pain and ROM.
Cochrane Handbook chapter. Not a primary study.
Retrospective study of treatment response, not an RCT or quasi-RCT.
RCT comparing two mobilization techniques (Mulligan vs Maitland) for adhesive capsulitis. Meets criteria: RCT, population, manual therapy comparison.
Cochrane Handbook chapter. Not a primary study.
Observational study on consultation prevalence. Not an RCT on adhesive capsulitis treatment.
RCT on iontophoresis vs phonophoresis for shoulder periarthritis. Neither intervention is manual therapy or exercise; these are electrotherapy modalities. Does not meet intervention criteria.

Prospective randomised observer-blind trial with 62 patients with painful stiff shoulder (periarthritis). Compares local steroids, 6 weeks physiotherapy, or both. Meets criteria: RCT, relevant population, physiotherapy includes exercise/manual therapy.

RCT with 70 subjects with frozen shoulder. Both intervention groups received shoulder exercises plus either electroacupuncture or interferential electrotherapy vs control. Exercise is a core component of the interventions. Meets criteria: RCT, population, includes exercise; outcomes include pain and function.

RCT with 122 subjects with adhesive capsulitis. Compares physical therapy (a combined technique) plus ibuprofen vs ibuprofen alone. Meets criteria: RCT, population, includes manual therapy/exercise; outcomes include SPADI, global rating.

RCT with 22 patients with adhesive capsulitis. Compares exercises and ultrasound vs exercises, ultrasound, and end-range mobilization. Meets criteria: RCT, population, manual therapy (mobilization) plus exercise; outcomes include pain and ROM.

RCT with 20 subjects with adhesive capsulitis. Compares anterior vs posterior mobilization techniques plus ultrasound and exercise. Meets criteria: RCT, population, mobilization; outcomes include ROM and pain.

RCT with 80 patients with adhesive capsulitis. Compares triamcinolone injection, physiotherapy (standardized physiotherapy including manual therapy/exercise), combination, and placebo. All had home exercise. Meets criteria: RCT, population, manual therapy/exercise; outcomes include disability, pain, ROM.

RCT (prospective randomised) with 72 patients with adhesive capsulitis. Compares manipulation under anaesthesia (manual therapy), peri-articular injection, and physiotherapy (exercise/mobilization). Meets criteria: RCT, population, manual therapy/exercise.
Systematic review, not a primary RCT. Will be used for reference but not screened as a candidate study.
Book chapter. Not a primary study.

The abstract describes a prospective investigation of 120 patients where outcomes were compared by age, gender, handedness, duration, frequency of joint mobilization, and self-exercise compliance. This is not a randomized comparison of intervention arms; it is an observational analysis of predictors. Does not meet design criteria.

Prospective, systematically allocated clinical trial (likely quasi-randomised). 8 subjects with adhesive capsulitis. Compares high-velocity manipulation + exercise vs mobilization + exercise. Meets criteria: RCT/quasi-RCT, population, manual therapy + exercise comparison; outcomes include SPADI.
RCT with 100 subjects with adhesive capsulitis. Compares high-grade vs low-grade mobilization techniques. Meets criteria: RCT, population, manual therapy; outcomes include ROM, disability.

RCT (single-blinded, experimental, pilot study) with 14 subjects with shoulder capsulitis. Compares home-care programme vs home-care programme plus passive mobilisation. Meets criteria: RCT, population, manual therapy; outcomes include pain, function, ROM.
